howToUse: This is your Reframe Script Bank — a ready-to-deploy collection of self-coaching prompts and perspective-shift scripts for the exact moments when your brain tells you it isn't wired for this. Open it the second you hit a stuck moment (blank page, rewrite spiral, post-publish dread), find the script that matches where you are, say it out loud or write it in your doc, and keep moving. Nothing to learn first — just find your moment and use the words.
promise: These seventeen scripts hand you the exact words to redirect the "I'm not a writer" fear in real time, so the stuck moment becomes a five-second reset instead of a two-hour avoidance spiral. Use them alongside the programme work and the blank page stops being a verdict about your talent.
tools:
[
  {
    "name": "The 17-Script Reframe Bank (Indexed by Stuck Moment)",
    "type": "swipe",
    "instructions": "Find the stuck moment that matches where you are right now. Read the script once — out loud if possible. Then open your doc and write the next sentence.",
    "content": "# The 17-Script Reframe Bank

---

## STUCK MOMENT A — The Blank Page
*You've opened a new document. The cursor is blinking. Nothing is coming.*

**Script 1**
I don't need to write a sales page right now — I need to write the next sentence. One sentence is all I'm being asked for.

**Script 2**
I've described this offer out loud to a client and watched their face change. That conversation is still in me. I'm not starting from nothing — I'm translating.

**Script 3**
The first draft isn't copy. It's a voice memo typed with my fingers. Nothing that goes in this document right now has to stay.

**Script 4**
I know this person. I know the exact moment they ran out of their own answer. I'm going to write to that moment, not to the whole problem.

**Script 5**
The page feels high-stakes because I care about the offer. That's the same feeling I have at the start of a powerful discovery call — and I know how those end.

---

## STUCK MOMENT B — The Rewrite Spiral
*You've written something. Now you've rewritten it eleven times and it's getting worse, not better.*

**Script 6**
I am not making this better right now. I am just making it different. I'm going to leave the last version and move to the next section.

**Script 7**
Perfect copy doesn't exist before it's been read by a real person. What I'm calling 'not right yet' is actually 'not tested yet.' Those are different problems.

**Script 8**
The sentence I keep rewriting is not broken — I'm trying to make it do too many jobs. What is the one thing this sentence needs to say?

**Script 9**
I can hold a prospect on a discovery call and have them say 'you completely get me' in fifteen minutes. That skill is not different from this — it's the same read of a person, put on the page. I already have the instinct. I'm building the form.

**Script 10**
I know what my best client would say if this sentence landed right. I'm going to write for her, not for the imaginary reader who is trying to catch me out.

---

## STUCK MOMENT C — The Talent Verdict
*The quiet voice that says: 'Other people can write. You are not one of them. This investment is about to confirm that.'*

**Script 11**
Writing copy is a skill, not a trait. The coaches I admire who write well were not born doing it — they practised. I am currently practising.

**Script 12**
The evidence I'm using to decide I can't write is a draft — not a finished piece, not a published page, not a real prospect's response. I'm calling my rough work a verdict.

**Script 13**
I am not bad at writing. I am new at writing in this specific form. I am very good at several things I was once new at.

**Script 14**
The reason my copy hasn't converted yet is not that I lack talent — it's that I haven't yet learned which specific psychological moment in my buyer's journey is doing the conversion work. That is a knowledge gap, not a wiring problem. Knowledge gaps close.

---

## STUCK MOMENT D — The Post-Publish Spiral
*You've hit send or gone live. Now the regret is setting in — every phrase suddenly sounds wrong.*

**Script 15**
The page is live. The only thing publishing it confirmed is that I finish things. That is the skill most coaches never build.

**Script 16**
I cannot learn what doesn't convert until I have something in the market. This page is data, not a report card.

**Script 17**
I wrote this in my own voice. If a prospect reads it and says 'this really resonated' — and they will — I'll know it was mine that did it. That's what I'm building toward."
  },
  {
    "name": "The Stuck-Moment Diagnostic Worksheet",
    "type": "worksheet",
    "instructions": "Fill this in the moment you realise you've stopped — before you close the laptop. Takes under three minutes and tells you exactly which script to reach for.",
    "content": "# Stuck-Moment Diagnostic Worksheet
*Complete this before you close the laptop or switch tabs.*

---

## Step 1 — Name the moment (circle one)

| Code | Stuck Moment | What it feels like |
|------|-------------|--------------------|
| A | Blank page | The cursor is blinking. I have nothing. |
| B | Rewrite spiral | I've rewritten this same section more than three times. |
| C | Talent verdict | A quiet voice is telling me I'm simply not wired for this. |
| D | Post-publish spiral | It's live and I already hate it. |

**My current stuck moment is:** [A / B / C / D]

---

## Step 2 — Write the sentence that's blocking you
*(The exact thought your brain is producing right now — don't edit it.)*

> [WRITE THE BLOCKING THOUGHT HERE]

---

## Step 3 — Locate the Script Bank section that matches your letter
Turn to that section. Pick the script that feels closest to the blocking thought above.

**Script number I'm using:** [____]

---

## Step 4 — Write the script out in your own handwriting or type it into your doc
*(Copying it activates it — reading alone is not enough.)*

**The script, in my words:**
> [WRITE OR PASTE THE SCRIPT HERE]

---

## Step 5 — Set a ten-minute timer and write one thing
Not the whole page. Not the whole section. One sentence, one bullet, one opening line. When the timer ends, check: are you still stopped?

**What I wrote in ten minutes:**
> [WRITE IT HERE — even if it's rough]

---

*If you're still stopped after Step 5: this is not a talent problem. Go back to Step 1 and pick the next closest stuck moment code. The block has shifted — find the new one.*"

  {
    "name": "The Discovery-Call-to-Copy Translation SOP",
    "type": "sop",
    "instructions": "Run this SOP once before you start any new piece of copy — sales page, email, or invitation. It converts the instinct you already use on discovery calls into raw copy material before the blank page appears.",
    "content": "# The Discovery-Call-to-Copy Translation SOP
*Run this before you open a blank document. It takes 20–25 minutes and produces raw material you can write from immediately.*

---

## Why this works
You already know how to read a prospect accurately and have them feel understood within fifteen minutes on a call. That skill — locating the specific moment they ran out of their own answer — is exactly the skill that makes copy convert. This SOP makes that instinct visible and usable on the page.

---

## What you need
- A voice recorder (phone is fine) or a blank document
- 20–25 minutes of uninterrupted time
- Memory of one real discovery call or client conversation that went well

---

## The SOP

**Step 1 — Pick one real client or prospect (3 min)**
Don't composite. Choose the one person where the call felt like the most accurate conversation — the one where they said something like "how did you know that?" or "you completely get it."

Write their first name here (or a code name): **[CLIENT NAME / CODE]**

---

**Step 2 — Locate the mid-sentence stop (5 min)**
Think back to that call. There was a specific moment — not a general problem, but a single sentence they couldn't finish, a single situation where they ran out of their own answer.

Write it out as they said it, as close to verbatim as you can:
> "[THEIR WORDS — the moment they stopped, the sentence they couldn't finish, the situation they described]"

This is the moment your copy needs to locate. Not their category of pain — this exact moment.

---

**Step 3 — Say out loud what you said next (5 min)**
On the call, you responded to that moment with something that landed. Record yourself saying what you said — or write it exactly as you would say it, not as you would type it.

> [YOUR RESPONSE — the words you used on the call that made them exhale]

This is a line of copy. You may not recognise it yet, but it is.

---

**Step 4 — Translate to page position (5 min)**
Every section of a sales page or email maps to a moment in the buyer's journey. Decide where the moment from Step 2 belongs:

| Page section | What it needs to do |
|-------------|--------------------|
| Opening line | Make the right person feel caught, accurately |
| Problem section | Name the specific stuck moment, not the general pain |
| Solution intro | Connect what you offer to the moment they ran out of answers |
| Call to action | Tell them what happens the moment they say yes |

**The moment I found in Step 2 belongs in:** [SECTION NAME]

**The words from Step 3 belong in:** [SECTION NAME]

---

**Step 5 — Write from the material, not from scratch (5 min)**
Open your copy document. Paste your Step 2 and Step 3 answers in. Start the next sentence from there.

You are not staring at a blank page. You are extending a conversation you already know how to have.

---

*Repeat this SOP for each section of a page where you hit a blank. Each section has its own moment — find that moment first, then write.*"

  {
    "name": "The 'This Is Still Me' Post-Publish Reset Checklist",
    "type": "checklist",
    "instructions": "Run this within 24 hours of publishing any piece of copy — sales page, email, or invitation — when the post-publish spiral starts. Go through it in order. Stop when the spiral stops.",
    "content": "# The 'This Is Still Me' Post-Publish Reset Checklist
*For the 24 hours after you hit send or go live, when every word suddenly sounds wrong.*

---

## Before you run this checklist — confirm:
- [ ] The copy is live / sent and cannot be unpublished in the next hour without real cost
- [ ] You have no actual prospect feedback yet (only your own rereading)

If both are true: the spiral is internal, not informational. Continue.

---

## The Reset Sequence

**1. Name what you're actually afraid of**
Circle the real fear:
- [ ] A — A real person will read this and think less of me
- [ ] B — This doesn't sound like my voice
- [ ] C — This won't convert and I'll have to face that
- [ ] D — I made a mistake I can't fix

---

**2. Check the fear against the evidence available to you right now**

| Fear | What evidence do you actually have right now? |
|------|----------------------------------------------|
| A — Someone will think less of me | [ ] No real responses yet — this is imagined, not reported |
| B — Doesn't sound like my voice | [ ] Could you read one paragraph aloud without stumbling? If yes: it's your voice. |
| C — Won't convert | [ ] Has any qualified prospect seen it yet? No data = no verdict. |
| D — Made a fixable mistake | [ ] Is the mistake factual (wrong date, wrong link)? Fix it. If it's a word choice: leave it. |

---

**3. Apply the correct Script Bank script**

| Fear code | Script to use |
|-----------|---------------|
| A | Script 17 |
| B | Script 9 or Script 17 |
| C | Script 16 |
| D | Script 15 |

Write the script out: **[COPY SCRIPT HERE]**

---

**4. Set a 48-hour data window**
You cannot evaluate copy without real-person responses. Write the date and time 48 hours from now:

**I will look at real data at:** [DATE] at [TIME]

Until then: the copy is live, it is doing its job, and your job is to let it run.

---

**5. The one thing you are allowed to fix right now**
- [ ] A broken link
- [ ] A factual error (wrong date, wrong name, wrong price)
- [ ] A typo in the subject line or headline

Anything else: **not now.** Edits made during the spiral make copy worse, not better.

---

**6. Final check — say this out loud:**
*"I wrote this in my own voice. It is in the market. I will know more in 48 hours than I know right now."*

- [ ] Said it

---

*When real data arrives at the 48-hour window, take it to the Client Psychology Reverse-Map framework in the programme. That's where you make evidence-based edits — not here, not tonight.*"
  }
